findings.title: Storage init failures now abort NewResourceServer and block startup on the full index build
findings.body: NewResourceServer now calls s.Init synchronously. Init runs lifecycle.Init (DB connect and ping) and the search init, which builds an index for every namespace above InitMinCount, and returns the error to the caller. Previously these failures only surfaced as errors on the first gRPC call and never stopped construction. Now a transient DB error or any index build error makes the constructor fail, which fails whatever wires the server, and startup (including HTTP and metrics) is blocked for the entire index build. Init is also never retried. This is the behavior change the PR description asks about. It should be called out explicitly, and the module init order should be checked to confirm the DB and dependencies are ready when the provider runs.

findings.title: On-demand index build still runs under the gRPC request context
findings.body: getOrCreateIndex still builds a missing index with the request context: s.build(ctx, key, 10, 0). The build's ListIterator and builder calls use that ctx. Namespaces at or below InitMinCount at startup are not indexed at init. If such a namespace has since grown, the first Search builds the whole index inside the RPC, and a client cancel or deadline aborts the build mid-way. The index is then never cached, so the same failure repeats on every request. This is the failure mode the PR says it fixes, and it remains on this path. The fixed size hint of 10 also always selects the memory-only index.

findings.title: Removing the BuildIndex lock allows concurrent duplicate builds for the same key
findings.body: BuildIndex no longer serializes builds: the lock was removed from the whole function and only the final cache write is locked. Nothing deduplicates concurrent builds for one key, and getOrCreateIndex's GetIndex-then-build sequence is not atomic. Two concurrent cold Search or watch-event calls for the same namespace now build two full indexes in parallel, roughly doubling memory and CPU. The second 'b.cache[key] = idx' silently replaces the first index, which is never closed. For file-backed indexes, the second bleve.New on the same directory races the first and can fail. The previous code built twice too, but serially. Use per-key singleflight or re-check under the lock.

findings.title: TotalDocs iterates the cache map without holding cacheMu
findings.body: TotalDocs ranges over b.cache with no lock, while GetIndex takes RLock and BuildIndex writes the map under Lock. The new log line in search.go init (line 216) calls TotalDocs after the watch goroutine has started (lines 207-213). That goroutine can call handleEvent, then getOrCreateIndex, then BuildIndex, which writes the map concurrently. A concurrent map iteration and write is a fatal runtime error in Go and cannot be recovered. TotalDocs should take cacheMu.RLock().

findings.title: Data race on shared err and counter in the parallel init workers
findings.body: Pre-existing, but it is in the function being edited. The errgroup closure assigns the outer function's err variable ('_, _, err = s.build(...)') and increments totalBatchesIndexed (line 189), and both run concurrently in up to initWorkers goroutines. That is an unsynchronized write from multiple goroutines, which the race detector flags and which can tear an interface value. The closure should use a local error (the return value already reaches group.Wait), and the counter should be atomic.

findings.title: GetResourceStats never checks rows.Err, so a mid-iteration failure returns partial stats as success
findings.body: The loop ends when rows.Next() returns false. If that was caused by an error (for example a dropped connection), rows.Err() holds it, but the code never checks it. The callback then returns err, which is nil at that point, and the function returns partial res with a nil error. search init then indexes only the namespaces that were read, logs success, and never retries. rows is also not closed on the early Scan-error return. Check rows.Err() after the loop and defer rows.Close().

findings.title: Trace propagation fixed only in GetResourceStats; sibling methods still drop the span context
findings.body: The PR says it fixes trace propagation, but only GetResourceStats was changed. WriteEvent (line 158), ReadResource (line 353) and ListIterator (line 388) still do '_, span := b.tracer.Start(ctx, ...)' and then pass the parent ctx down. As a result the create, update and delete spans and the DB transaction spans are siblings of the wrapper span, not children. bleve.go BuildIndex (line 88) has the same pattern. Either finish the change in these methods or narrow the PR description.

findings.title: Removing the Init gate from every RPC silently allows requests after Stop
findings.body: Before this change, each RPC called s.Init, which returned s.initErr. Stop sets initErr to 'service is stopped', so every request after Stop was rejected. With the gates removed, initErr is dead state and RPCs keep being served after Stop, even though the broadcaster context has been cancelled. This behavior change is not mentioned in the PR. Either keep a stopped check in the RPCs or document the change.

findings.title: Postgres skip removes the only startup test for the storage target in CI
findings.body: The new skip disables the only test that exercises starting the storage-server target, for postgres, with a TODO and the reason 'Works locally'. This PR changes exactly that startup path, because Init now runs inside NewResourceServer. CI therefore has no coverage of the new startup behavior on postgres. The PR description does not mention this test change. Either fix the test or track the skip with an issue and explain why the change is safe.

findings.title: NewResourceServer leaks its context and started goroutines when Init fails
findings.body: The context and cancel func are created at line 229, but on the Init error path the constructor returns without calling s.cancel(). If initWatcher failed after the broadcaster started, its goroutines keep running on s.ctx. The lifecycle hooks, which may already have been initialized, are not stopped either. The same applies to the error return at line 254. Call s.cancel() (and stop the lifecycle) before returning the error.

findings.title: Watcher goroutine dereferences nil event when the backend stops, panicking at shutdown
findings.body: Pre-existing, but in the function being edited. When the backend stops, the poller returns and runs 'defer close(stream)'. The loop 'v := <-events' then receives nil forever, and handleEvent reads evt.Type on a nil pointer, which panics and crashes the process during shutdown. The same pattern exists in server.go initWatcher (around lines 762-765, where v.Type is read). Use 'v, ok := <-events' and return when !ok.
